log.what: Your 24 requests received. Branch v5-live-game created from the V4 tip (f1b9a4cf).

Mapped the current game with three read-only searches (content and balance; menu, backend and web3; art) and two web research tasks (survivor-like balance; Solana, MagicBlock, wallets and multiplayer). Research saved in plan/v5/research/.
Independent reviewer agent written: .claude/agents/v5-reviewer.md (read-only; reviews the plan and each phase's code).
Baseline in the open Editor: EditMode 307/307, PlayMode 49/49, console clean.
Plan written: 26 phases in six stages, 14 proposed decisions, 20 questions for you.

Independent plan review: 3 blockers, 12 majors, 7 minors. All fixed in plan rev 2: a replay-verification spike before accounts, pending RUM until verified, no RUM-to-token bridge through items, anti-collusion rules, wager formats per mode, split phases (now 29, M0–M28). Details under Review findings.
GDD updated: three Decision log rows (V5 direction, reversals, two economies and custody), the roadmap's V5 track, the Not now and Never lists, and 27 V5 questions on the board.

Plan re-review of rev 2: no blockers, 5 majors and 6 minors (server-issued seeds, capped legacy RUM on migration, the fallback that would amend D6, two oversized phases, the real-time no-go path). All fixed in plan rev 3: M9b (conditional kinematic port), M10/M10b and M26/M26b splits, an early netcode measurement in M9.

Your answers to the V5 questions applied as plan rev 4: custody on our Railway server, a Monte Carlo balance simulator instead of autopilot runs, one enemy cap sized for a low-end phone, endless overtime, RUM treasury and vault, anti-collusion deferred, and more (decision D17). Researched and explained what you asked about: Photon and the other multiplayer options with costs, sign-in, hosting, Megabonk's levels, the four weapons plus eight more ideas, replay verification, and a cost breakdown of every third-party account (about $5–20 a month at 100 players). See Your answers, explained.

Independent review of your answers (rev 4): no blockers, 6 majors, 7 minors, all fixed in rev 5: custody safeguards (master-key backup and rotation, separate secrets, one-time key export), numeric pass limits for the Photon test in M9, the enemy cap set on your reference phone in M1, deferred anti-collusion switches still tested. Three new questions (Q31–Q33).

Your second round of answers applied as plan rev 7: 6 full-loot AI raids a day, uncapped PvP RUM, Google + email sign-in, Railway only, evolutions at level 8 with multi-level rare cards, nine new weapons (M4, M4b), a new Monte Carlo simulator written from scratch on V4 with ten player personalities, plausibility checks with value-moving modes played on our match server (moved up to M13b), no key export. Researched the 4-player Hunt netcode (recommendation now Fish-Net + Bayou: Photon calls its server mode "not recommended" for browsers) and the reference phone (Galaxy A15 / A16 4G at a steady 30 fps; browser memory near 256 MB is the big constraint).

Independent review of rev 7: no blockers, 8 majors, 10 minors, all fixed in rev 8: plausibility bounds from the balance model, a hard 256 MB mobile memory limit, a prediction-ready ship controller, server-session costs measured in M9 (Railway estimate ~$30–60/month once sessions run), the multi-ship lobby as its own phase (M21), fully specified personalities. Two new questions (Q34, Q35).

Your third round of answers applied as plan rev 9: Unity Netcode for GameObjects for multiplayer (free; we write nearby-enemy filtering and lag compensation), treasury protection (vault 80% / treasury 20%, 8 h shield, 10% daily loss cap, 72 h for new players), the reference phone (Galaxy A15 / A16 4G at 30 fps), forfeits pay nothing but a genuine short match does, checked voyage RUM usable on devnet. Every V5 question is now answered. Added a per-service Railway cost breakdown with savings (about $20–25/month if ~30 of 100 players play daily; $40–45 if all do; about $14–33 with the three biggest savings).
You chose: carry on while away, commit and push each phase that passes its tests and review, stand-in instead of the phone, Unity restarts allowed. M0 committed and pushed.

M1 enemy flow built (unattended): a minimum crowd per minute (ten 1-minute waves with a jagged floor), four telegraphed hordes (ring, line, pack) with a lull before each and edge markers, breathing room after arenas, the boss kill and hordes, a lower floor during the boss fight, XP that merges instead of being lost. Off under the v3-parity preset. Independent review: 3 blockers, 4 majors, 9 minors, all fixed. EditMode 331/331, PlayMode 50/50, playable check 0 game errors. Found: today's WebGL build needs a 344 MB heap and a 160 MB download, above the phone budget (moved to M7).

M2 balance model built (unattended): a Monte Carlo simulator written new on V4 (the real level-up, item and Captain code; ten player personalities), calibrated against the V4 autopilot's recorded runs (median death 7.8 vs 8.0 Observe, 6.4 vs 6.3 Adaptive). It found every personality sinking at the 2:30 Reef Crab, slow level-ups, a crowd stuck at the cap from 4:00, 1-second elites and overtime ending every run by ~13 min. Retuned: faster XP curve, a ~17 s Reef Crab, ~5.5 s elites, a ~55 s Barnacle King, gentler growth after 2:00, lower band rates from 4:00, a slower overtime ramp, the director's on-track curve re-measured. 72 of 76 revised targets met (66 of 76 of the first proposals). New F1 console Balance section. Review: 1 blocker (a boss HP change the game ignored), 7 majors, 8 minors; all fixed or recorded; second pass found 4 more, fixed.

M3 build balance built (unattended): evolutions reachable (the card from weapon level 8 with its item; Rare/Epic cards +2 levels, Legendary +3; a pity rule; a 40% chance that a chest gives a ready weapon's evolution item) — focused builds now evolve in ~60% of runs, around minute 6. All ten weapons within ±20% of their role at levels 1, 4, 8 and 12 (the Flamethrower no longer fades, the Powder Kegs no longer lag, the Lightning Mast no longer runs away). Plain Logbooks and items in their rarity bands; volley and crit pieces flagged; synergy items left for you. Captains within ±10% on run length (Flint's hull 90 → 120). 5 items by 10:00. Review: 3 majors, 10 minors, then 1 major and 3 minors on the fixes; all fixed or recorded.

Demo interlude, merged into V5: the art team's menu, Captain select, HUD and level-up cards; per-weapon, ship and enemy VFX profiles with an editor; POI and level-up card prefabs; music; the floating joystick (app and mobile browsers); safe-area HUD; mobile render settings (60 fps on a Pixel 9a); smarter enemies; shots stop at islands; APK and WebGL builds. Kept for V5: half XP, 1.625x ship speed, lower player ranges, the AI changes, cannon boats from 1:00, the boss rising out of a whirlpool after the beacon summon. Restored: POIs, Captain active, boost, barks, tutorial, Logbook cards, flamethrower. EditMode 367/367, PlayMode 51/51.

Balance re-check on the demo baseline: half XP and the 1.625x ship speed moved into config and the simulator. Half XP alone took the model from 2 of 76 to 24 of 70 targets missed; you kept it and chose a retune: enemy HP growth x0.55, damage growth x0.7, the evolution card from weapon level 6 (was 8), Lightning Mast -2%, the director curve re-measured, level and level-up targets at the slower pace. Result: 2 of 76 missed, the same two as M3; median run 10.3 min (10.1); levels about 40% slower. Review: no blockers, 10 minors, then 3 minors on the fixes; all fixed. EditMode 372/372, PlayMode 53/53. Details: plan/v5/balance-recheck/README.md.
Your answers: M1–M3 and the retune are fine for now (finetuning later), and the level-up pace targets hold the pace at ±20% (minute 1: 12–18 s; 0–10 min: 20–30 s).

You left notes a-k and a sketch before going away for 7-8 hours and asked me to keep going and decide on your behalf. Plan: four new phases before M4: M3b feel fixes, M3c level-up rhythm, M3d pressure from enemy count with peaks and valleys and distinct enemies, M3e performance and the enemy cap. Decisions and questions: plan/v5/DECISIONS-WHILE-AWAY.md. The plan review found no blockers, 7 majors and 5 minors, all fixed (M3c split, the cap after measuring, M3's evolution goals re-checked).

M3b feel fixes built (awaiting your playtest): an island hit pushes the ship back off the shore and costs 5 hull at most every 2 s (through Brace! and the Keel, with the usual hit flash); unblown powder kegs sink after 45 s; the Captain's special ability has a round touch button in the joystick's art above the weapon grid, with a cooldown sweep (touch devices only). Review: no blockers; 9 code findings and 4 more on the fixes, all fixed (the button and the Captain bar could hide for good; the bounce was being cancelled by the reverse-speed limit). EditMode 374/374, PlayMode 56/57 (a known intermittent test).

M3c level-up rhythm built (awaiting your playtest): your "1 1 2 3 5" as gaps of 10, 10, 20, 30, 50 s after the first kill, then 60 s: 4 level-ups in the first minute as before, about 13 by 10:00 (was ~24), through a per-level XP table fitted in the simulator. To keep builds strong with fewer picks: weapon cards grant 2/2/3/3/4 levels, evolutions from weapon level 5, Roxie's hull 104, and an interim flat enemy scale (×0.85) that M3d replaces. Simulator: 2 of 76 targets missed (the same two as M3), median run 10.6 min, focused builds evolve in 65% of runs. Review: one blocker (other personalities' boss wins) and several majors, all fixed and re-verified. EditMode 381/381, PlayMode 57/57.

M3d pressure from enemy count built (awaiting your playtest): enemy HP and damage no longer grow with time (a cannon boat has 12 HP at 1:00 and at 8:00); the crowd follows your sketch in 22 keyframes (small early peaks, a big one at 3:35-3:45, a long valley rising in ~60 s waves, peaks at 7:30 and 9:35); stronger late types at fixed stats; every enemy that attacks differently looks different (tint, size), and hordes are ordinary ships. Per-minute targets now come from the design, not the simulator. Simulator: 2 of 76 targets missed (the First-Timer, minute 6 kills in the boss fight), both bounded and listed (D22); median run 11.0 min; in 15 s bins the crowd peaks at 3:45 (about 44) over a quieter valley (about 34) and rises to 65-69 at 7:30 and 9:30. Review: 1 blocker (the curve did not follow the sketch) and 10 majors (targets fitted to measurements, overtime understated, a heavy model, hordes, the look test, hitboxes, tint code), all fixed; the second pass found 1 major (the crowd, not only the floor, must show the peak) and 6 minors, fixed or recorded. EditMode 397/397, PlayMode 59/59.

UI text without em dashes: about 60 toasts, prompts, menu labels and boss and tutorial texts now use a colon or a comma; the toast and the tutorial prompt clean any text that reaches them; a test guards it (D23).

M3e performance built (awaiting your playtest): measured on the same map, three runs a side in the Editor. The game's garbage fell from 28 KB to 1.3 KB a frame (the ship wakes searched every enemy's children every frame), the enemy world's main-thread time from 1.42 to 0.67 ms, batches at 9:00 from 991 to 784, triangles from 1.57M to 1.45M (Mesh LODs for 14 heavy models: one chest was ~77,650 triangles). Pools now make nothing mid-run and enemy models are stripped in the pool (a NavMesh warning fell from 99 to 2 a run). Static batching of the islands was tried and taken out (+25 MB for ~50 batches); dynamic batching gave nothing; occlusion culling does not apply here (the far clip went 1000 → 250 m instead). The enemy cap stays 80 until the reference phone (D24). Review: 1 blocker (plan items left unrecorded) and 5 majors, fixed or recorded (D27).

M4a and M4 built (awaiting your playtest): slow, pierce, knockback, several orbit weapons and boost-gated auras (today's ten weapons proved unchanged); four new weapons (Anchor Flail, Chainshot, Siren Bell, Ramming Prow) at 120-160 Rum; eight evolutions (one generic Empowered kind) with their chest items; damage set by the balance model within 20% of each role. Decisions D28-D31.

M4b built (awaiting your playtest): Parrot Squadron, Monkey Gunners, Maelstrom Charge, Lighthouse Lantern, Cursed Doubloons (170-220 Rum) with five Empowered evolutions and their items; pull, whirlpools, sweeping beams, capped summons and capped kill gold; the balance model and the difficulty director now share how many hits a firing deals (the Anchor Flail re-tuned with it). D32.

M5 built (awaiting your playtest): four Logbooks (Fortune, Tidecaller, Admiral, Plunderer; Ironclad waits for armor), thirteen items bought with Rum (Shark Tooth, Skeleton Key, Smuggler's Ledger, Black Spot, Barnacle Crown, Jolly Roger, Leviathan Heart, Captain's Last Rum and more); new item effects with tests. The free Commons and the four designed powerups would have pushed the balance bands, so they wait for you (D33, D34; questions 27-32).

M7 mobile UI and input built (awaiting your playtest): touch BOOST and PAUSE buttons, a pause menu (Escape, gamepad Start, touch) with Resume, Settings and Quit; Settings (UI scale, music, effects, quality, reduced effects, shake, stick side and dead zone) from the menu and the pause menu; safe-area wrapping; 72-unit touch targets; automatic quality; WebGL mobile and desktop build profiles and a LAN server. Review: no blockers, 7 majors and 8 minors, fixed or recorded. Three questions for you (33-35).

M8 menu hub and shop built (awaiting your playtest): SET SAIL opens a mode select (Voyage; Raids, Race, Arena, Hunt coming), LEDGER the shop (weapons, Logbooks, items, Captains for RUM), PROFILE your stats and collection; meta services (account, RUM, inventory, store) over the local save behind interfaces for the server. Content out of every pool is not sold. Review: no blockers, 4 majors and 6 minors, fixed or recorded. Questions 36-38.

The phone build (M7b): texture pass (881 textures capped at 1024 on WebGL), download 111 MB (163 MB in September). With 256 MB of heap it ran out of memory loading the menu, so it builds with 512 MB (D37, question 39). In a browser it reaches the menu, the mode select, the Captain select, a run and the pause menu. Serve it to your phone with python plan/v5/tools/serve-webgl.py "Pirate Game Unity/Builds/WebGL-Mobile/RoguePirates".

Phone performance, web (M7c): about 50 benchmark runs on your Pixel 9a over USB and a desktop Chrome found two costly systems and a texture bug. The minimap fog now redraws only around new cells (the regular 100+ ms freezes are gone), enemy health bars share one canvas, phones get ASTC textures. Phone with 80 enemies: 26.0 to 37.5 fps, slowest 1% of frames 144 to 42 ms; GPU memory 2.27 to 1.53 GB; download 111 to 87.5 MB. Desktop: locked 60 fps. Review: 1 blocker, 5 majors, 6 minors, fixed. Report: Rogue Pirates Phone Bench.

Android APK (M7d): the native app holds a locked 60 fps on the Pixel 9a in every variant, even with 80 enemies; Vulkan, GLES3 and frame pacing make no difference there (the default kept). An Android texture cap cut the APK from 155.5 to 127.9 MB and about 60 MB of memory. The playtest APK (126.9 MB) is installed on your phone. Review: no blockers, 4 majors, 9 minors, fixed.

Playtest rounds 5-7 (branch playtest): Survivor.io-style 15-minute voyage, Monte Carlo balance model (Saltwind Balance Simulator), weapon roles, armor, timed heals; guest profiles, weekly leaderboard and 1v1 PvP (lobby, invites, draft, relayed match, bot, rematch) on an API live on Railway; island hits only from real islands; attack warnings for non-projectile attacks, dark cannonballs; desktop WebGL build.

Playtest round 8: PvP draft descriptions and four PvP fixes, the opponent's health, attacks and loadout on both screens, health bars on elites, minibosses and the boss, fight floors and Barnacle King health halved, enemy damage +25%; independent review (no blockers, fixes applied); Android APK.

Round 9: Set Sail goes to the Captain select, side buttons widened; chests back, flamethrower back on; review fixes; Unity tests EditMode 438/499 and PlayMode 51/63 (one stale parity-preset entry had broken about 30 tests).

All points of interest and the Beacon boss summon back (no timed boss); PowerShell deploy script and a GitHub Action for the API; a session recorder and compare_session.mjs to check the simulator against your play; back-to-V5 review (3 blockers, M8z added, plan rev 10).

Your answers P1-P10 (D18): playtest merged into v5-live-game; everything unlocked for now; timed heals now drop in view; an early-summoned boss keeps its 14:00 hull; PvP anti-cheat on the server (weapon in draft, range, damage cap by level, accepted damage decides time-outs) and rematch retry; attack warnings in their own slots; API deployed to Railway. First recorded session compared with the simulator: islands did 54% of the damage, the 3:00 elite Hammerhead stalled the run, the simulator is far off (recalibration in M8z).

Island hits 3 hull at most every 4 s (were 10 every 2 s); arena fights pause the waves for at most 20 s and their floor is 2 s of DPS; health pickups back as before; raid economy B with 4-hour shields and server-authoritative Netcode recorded (D19); anti-cheat audit per weapon in progress.

Owner follow-ups: arena fights keep the waves paused until they end (the 20 s limit removed) and get an off-screen pointer (in progress); island hits 5 hull at most every 2 s; raid economy without the daily loss cap, new-player protection or revenge raid; deploys stay manual (the agent runs server/deploy.ps1); PvP range rule edge-case audit in progress.

M0.title: Tests
M0.text: Baseline green: EditMode 307/307 and PlayMode 49/49 in Unity 6000.3.11f1; no compile errors.

M0.title: Reviewer
M0.text: Agent file in place; it ran the plan review (below). In this session it runs through a general agent loading the same file; new sessions list it as v5-reviewer.

M0.title: Plan reviews
M0.text: Two independent reviews: rev 1 had 3 blockers, 12 majors, 7 minors; rev 2 had no blockers, 5 majors, 6 minors. All addressed in rev 3.

M1.title: What changed
M1.text: Ten 1-minute waves keep a minimum crowd alive (topped up one enemy every 0.35 s), four hordes (1:45 ring, 5:30 line, 7:40 pack, 9:15 ring) with a 10 s lull and edge markers, breathing room after big moments, XP merging. Data in the Saltwind timeline; the v3-parity preset turns it off.

M1.title: Tests
M1.text: EditMode 331/331 (24 new), PlayMode 50/50 (1 new: the crowd reaches each minute's floor in the real scene). Playable check with screenshots at 1, 3, 5:30, 6, 9 and 13 minutes: 0 game errors.

M1.title: Review
M1.text: 3 blockers (spawn gap, missing edge markers, stale evidence), 4 majors, 9 minors: all fixed. Table on this page under Review findings.

M1.title: Your playtest
M1.text: Play three runs (a weak, an average and a strong build). Does the crowd feel constant but changing minute to minute? Do the hordes (1:45, 5:30, 7:40, 9:15) read, with the arrow at the screen edge? Is there breathing room after the Reef Crab, the elites and the boss? F1 → Wave Timeline shows the flow line.

M2.title: What changed
M2.text: Level-ups much faster (about every 8.6 s in minute 1, 17.7 s on average to 10:00; level ~34 at 10:00). The Reef Crab is a ~17 s fight (was ~50 s and sank almost everyone), elites take ~5.5 s, the Barnacle King ~55 s. Enemies grow more gently after 2:00, bands spawn a little slower from 4:00, overtime ramps more slowly (still endless). The v3-parity preset restores every old value.

M2.title: Tests
M2.text: EditMode 352/352, PlayMode 50/50. Model report: 72 of 76 revised targets (66 of 76 of the first proposals). Playable check: 0 game errors, the crowd inside its band at 1, 3, 6 and 9 minutes.

M2.title: Your decisions
M2.text: Which targets stand (nine were widened after the first run; both counts are on the M2 page); whether the Turtle ('careful survivor', but it dodges less than the average player and sinks earlier) should change; whether 6:00's crowd on the band ceiling is fine.

M2.title: Your playtest
M2.text: Three runs. Do level-ups arrive at a good pace (roughly every 8 s at first, then every 15-20 s)? Is the Reef Crab a real but short fight? Do elites feel tougher (4-8 s) and the Barnacle King a proper fight? Does the late voyage feel powerful rather than drowning? F1 → Balance → Run model shows the targets, the model and your run on one graph.

M3.title: What changed
M3.text: Evolutions: the card from weapon level 8 with its item, rarer cards grant 2–3 levels, a pity rule, and chests favour a ready weapon's evolution item. Weapons rebalanced within their roles (base damage and how fast upgrades grow). Gunnery Manual, Carpenter's Notes and Dragon's Breath Nozzle retuned; chest prices steeper (5 items by 10:00); Flint's hull 90 → 120. The v3-parity preset restores every old value.

M3.title: Tests

reviews.title: Plan review, rev 1 → rev 2 (29 Sep)
reviews.summary: The independent reviewer read the plan against your 24 requests, the research, the handoff rules, the GDD's never list and the current code. It found 3 blockers, 12 majors and 7 minors, and confirmed that the plan's claims about the existing code were accurate. All 22 are addressed in rev 2 (now 29 phases, M0–M28). A second review checks the fixes.

rows.finding: Server RUM trusted a client-uploaded run summary before any verification existed, against D6 and the handoff's rule on client-trust fallbacks.
rows.fix: Run RUM is now pending until verified and cannot be spent, transferred or wagered (D6, I10b.4).

rows.finding: Replay verification was assumed, not proven: unseeded draws (PickupModule, WorldPort), Rigidbody physics, no cost measured.
rows.fix: New M9 replay verification spike before accounts: seeding fixes, WebGL vs headless agreement over 10 runs, CPU per minute, go/no-go with named fallbacks (Q29).

rows.finding: RUM-bought items could be minted and sold for tokens: an indirect RUM-to-token bridge.
rows.fix: D4 now tracks item origin: anything bought, earned or traded with RUM stays web2 forever; island sales return RUM-bought parts to the seller (Q24).

rows.finding: The list of reversals missed token winnings (play-to-earn), token balances and the Arena draft.
rows.fix: D8 names all six reversals; Q26 asks you to confirm them.

rows.finding: NFT migration was planned before NFTs exist; royalty allow-lists block transfers by unlisted programs.
rows.fix: M13 migrates tokens, records and inventory; NFT migration moves to M26 through the game program.

rows.finding: No ownership sync for NFTs sold elsewhere; devnet external markets unconfirmed.
rows.fix: M26 adds an indexer or webhook with a reconcile job, and an honest devnet exit criterion (Tensor's open program).

rows.finding: No anti-collusion policy.
rows.fix: New D15 (linked accounts blocked, price bands, daily caps, review flags) wired into M15, M24, M26, M27; defaults in Q27.

rows.finding: Race and Hunt wager formats were undefined.
rows.fix: M24 defines Arena, Hunt and Race formats: entry windows, minimum entrants, refunds, unverified finishes.

rows.finding: A web3 playtest bought a decoration before decorations exist; phone measurement before the mobile build; an unrealistic hackathon option.
rows.fix: Playtest buys a store item; the cap is measured on desktop in M1 and on a phone in M7; Q1 option B rewritten.

rows.finding: The planned brain reused DevTools autopilots that never ship.
rows.fix: M16 rewrites the brain in Runtime with a test that Runtime never references DevTools (D10).

rows.finding: Player schedules stored as the designer-owned timeline asset (read as a singleton, hashed).
rows.fix: A schedule DTO in the base snapshot becomes an in-memory overlay at raid start; its hash enters raid records.

rows.finding: M1 and the old netcode-plus-Arena phase were too big for one gate.
rows.fix: Split: M1 enemy flow and M2 balance model; M21 netcode spike and M22 Arena.

rows.finding: Several phases lacked a playtest line or an automated check.
rows.fix: Every phase now has both (or an owner check for document and spike phases).

rows.finding: The .NET 8 target ends support on 10 Nov 2026.
rows.fix: The server moves to .NET 10 LTS in M10.

rows.finding: Raid loot currency undefined.
rows.fix: New question Q23 (suggested: RUM, split into an exposed treasury and a safe vault).

rows.finding: Wrong question numbers in two tasks.
rows.fix: Fixed in rev 2.

rows.finding: Siren Bell was said to charm; Grapeshot is an item, not a weapon.
rows.fix: Siren Bell slows and stuns; Grapeshot removed from the weapon options.

rows.finding: Onchain record rent and scope undefined.
rows.fix: Only value-bearing results are recorded; ordinary runs batch into the player record; match accounts close after settlement.

rows.finding: Web push needs a Firebase account, against the local-only rule.
rows.fix: D11 now covers third-party accounts; Q30 asks when to create them.

rows.finding: The v3-parity preset's status was unclear.
rows.fix: D16: it stays as a regression baseline until M28; new mechanics switch off under it.

rows.finding: Privy's server-held custody flow was unclear.
rows.fix: Q3 and M10/M11 spell out Privy server wallets with a server-verified token.

rows.finding: 'Saltwind only' narrowed the global kill board.
rows.fix: Option A is now every voyage biome as it ships.
